Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of Australia's reply. The floodlights are just about taking effect as the players make their way out to the middle. It will be the dynamic left-hand, right-hand combination of Travis Head and Mitchell Marsh to open the innings for Australia. Mohammed Siraj will start the attack for India. Marsh to face the first ball. Two slips in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The target isn't a big one but is competitive enough for the bowlers to have a go at the Aussies. Will India be able to defend this target, or will the Aussies chase this and clinch the series? Let's find out with the chase coming up in a bit.

The Australian bowlers were top-notch, and Marsh's decision to use 8 bowlers showcased his team's depth. Xavier Bartlett and Adam Zampa's wicket-taking ability was impressive as they took 3 and 4, respectively. Mitchell Starc's crucial wicket of Rohit was important for the stage it came at. Starc too picked up 2. Not to forget about Josh Hazlewood, whose spell was instrumental in setting up opportunities for others, even if the wickets didn't fall to him. The way the bowlers complemented each other's efforts was key to Australia's success.

The 118-run stand between Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer was the highlight of India's innings. However, after the 8th wicket fell at 226, scoring 250 runs seemed like an uphill task. Fortunately, a late flurry of runs from Harshit Rana and Arshdeep Singh, who added 37 for the 9th wicket, helped India push past 260. Now, the visitors will bank on their bowlers to make up for the batting unit's shortcomings and defend this total. India, despite not being at their best, goes into the break with a bit of momentum.

India's batting performance has been a mixed bag, managing 264 after being put in to bat. The top order was shaky, with Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli failing to make an impact. Rohit Sharma struggled initially but managed to survive and went on to score 73, while Shreyas Iyer played a solid knock of 61. Axar Patel too chipped in with a useful 44.

A leg bye to end the Indian innings! Full and sliding onto the pads. Mohammed Siraj swings to get this one away with the angle but fails to lay any bat on it. The ball catches the pads and dribbles in the square leg region. Adam Zampa gets to the ball quickly from short fine leg and keeps the batters down to one. India finish with 264 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Time for a drinks break. India's certainly having a tough time, scoring just 46/2 in 14 overs. Shubman Gill's dismissal was a setback, and Virat Kohli's back-to-back ducks haven't helped either. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get underway in front of what is being reported as a sell-out crowd. The sun is shining in all its glory as the two umpires make their way out to the centre. Mitchell Marsh leads his troops out, and they are followed by the two Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill. Mitchell Starc needs some repair work done on his shoes. He is now all set to kickstart proceedings for Australia. Starc to Rohit. Two slips in place. Off we go...

Well, Mitchell Marsh, at the toss, forgot to mention that Adam Zampa also comes into the side. Zampa replaces left-arm spinner Matthew Kuhnemann. So, three changes in total for Australia in today’s game, with Alex Carey and Xavier Bartlett being the other two inclusions.

The Indian skipper, Shubman Gill says that he would have bowled first as well. Feels that since the pitch has been under covers for the past couple of days, there could be some moisture. Mentions that it is never easy in a start-stop game but hopes to put a good total on the board here. He also hopes for some movement for their pacers under lights. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

The captain of Australia, Mitchell Marsh says that they will bowl first. Marsh expresses his excitement about the opportunity to win the series in the second game, highlighting the presence of young talent in the squad. He also mentions that the team has made two changes, with Alex Carey replacing Josh Philippe and Xavier Bartlett coming in for Nathan Ellis, who is being rested.

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (C), Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (WK), Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj.

Australia (Playing XI) - Mitchell Marsh (C), Travis Head, Matthew Short, Matt Renshaw, Alex Carey (WK) (In for Josh Philippe), Cooper Connolly, Mitchell Owen, Xavier Bartlett (In for Nathan Ellis), Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa (In for Matthew Kuhnemann), Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Shane Watson is near the deck. Shares that it is always a nice cricket surface here in Adelaide. Watson takes a close look and finds the wicket to be rock-hard. Believes that there will be a bit of moisture and, as a result, there will be a bit of grip off the seam, something the team batting first will have to be wary of. Further says that once the batters get through that early phase, there are runs to be had with the short square boundaries.

The return of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma has boosted India, but their rustiness was evident in the first ODI. Kohli's impressive record at the Adelaide Oval, where he has scored five centuries, will have the Aussies on alert. With India's top four looking to bounce back after a disappointing start to the series, this match could be a turning point. The battle between India's batting lineup and Australia's bowling attack will be a key aspect of the match. Australia's bowlers, led by Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, will be looking to build on their good work in the first ODI. Can Australia continue their dominance, or will India stage a comeback to level the series? Stick around to find out.

Australia will make some changes to their lineup, with Adam Zampa and Alex Carey returning. Josh Inglis, however, will miss this match due to a calf injury. India, on the other hand, doesn't have any injuries to report, but there could be some selection debates, with Kuldeep Yadav and Prasidh Krishna not selected for the series opener. A potential spot in the playing XI could be up for grabs between Kuldeep and Washington Sundar in the spin department and Krishna and Harshit Rana as far as the seam options are concerned.

A warm welcome to all cricket fans as we gear up for the second ODI between Australia and India at the Adelaide Oval. The stage is set for a thrilling encounter between two of the world's top cricketing nations, with Australia looking to seal the series with a game to spare. After a convincing 7-wicket win in the first ODI, the Aussies will be confident of their chances, but India will be eager to bounce back and level the series.

'Can the Men in Blue strike back, or will the Aussies tighten their grip on home soil?' - that’s the big question as the action shifts to the Adelaide Oval for the second ODI of this blockbuster series. After a forgettable outing in the opening game, India will be itching to find their rhythm again, especially with the top order yet to click and the middle order craving stability. The visitors will bank on the experience of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to lead the charge, while Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer will look to convert their starts into something substantial. KL Rahul has been consistently scoring runs in recent times, while the all-round abilities of Axar Patel will be crucial as well. Their bowling, spearheaded by Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh, will need early breakthroughs to challenge an Australian lineup brimming with intent. Kuldeep Yadav and Washington Sundar add good depth to the spin attack, but they will have to be at their absolute best to make an impact on this Adelaide wicket. The hosts, meanwhile, will be buoyed by their disciplined bowling display and a composed chase in the first ODI. Even without Pat Cummins, their attack looks potent with Josh Hazlewood’s precision, Mitchell Starc's express pace, and Nathan Ellis’s clever variations, while the likes of Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, who scored a half-century, and Matthew Short provide the firepower up top. Also, Alex Carey and Adam Zampa are back in the mix for this game, which makes them an even stronger unit. With Adelaide known for its true surface and high-scoring potential, both teams will fancy their chances, but for India, it’s about bouncing back strong and keeping the series alive, while Australia aim to seal it with authority and continue their home dominance. Whose side are you on?
